newsitem.title: USA: Shares in Bells, GTE advance broadly.
newsitem.headline: Shares in Bells, GTE advance broadly.

text.p: Regional Bell telephone stocks were two to four percent firmer by early afternoon on Wednesday on news of Tuesday's successful legal challenge to Federal Communication Commission regulations, analysts said.
"(The legal challenge) improves the probability for getting higher prices to resell local networks than under the FCC guidance," said Bette Massick of brokers Bear Stearns.
GTE Corp was separately 2-1/4 firmer at 40-7/8 by 1245 EDT/1645 GMT on strong third quarter results, she said.
"GTE saw very good demand, with access lines up 7.4 percent from a year ago," Massick said.

A U.S. court on Tuesday put on hold FCC pricing provisions for implementing part of the 1996 Telecommunications Act which allowed long distance companies, regional Bells and cable TV companies to compete in each other's markets.
The court's action puts back in the hands of state regulators, pending an FCC appeal, the responsibility to set prices to resell Bell circuits to new competitors.
Analysts said the FCC pricing guidance was for bigger discounts on the retail prices of local circuits than the states are likely to grant.
